nodes.text: son of Ingjald, son of Frodi. His mother was Thora,
daughter of Sigurd Snake-in-the-Eye. Sigurd's mother was Aslaug,
daughter of Sigurd the Slayer of Fafnir. Thorgeir Havarsson was
cousin of Thorgils Arason. Thorgeir and Thormod grew up in
Isafjord, and early on there was friendship between them,
that the one of them should avenge the other who lived
longer. But though people were then called Christians,
Christianity was still young at that time, and very imperfect, so that
many sparks of heathendom were still left then, and into bad customs
settled. That custom had been kept by famous
men who made that compact between themselves, that the one should
avenge the other who lived longer: they were to go
under three *jarðarmen* [turf arches; literally 'earth-necklaces'], and that was their oath. That rite
was done in this way: three strips of turf were to be cut out of
the earth, long ones. Their ends were all to stay fast
in the earth, and the loops raised up, so that people could
walk under them. That rite Thormod
and Thorgeir performed in their compact. Thormod was somewhat
older, but Thorgeir was the stronger. Their rise became
There was a woman called Grima, who lived at the farm at Ogur,
as it is called. She was a widow and well off. It was
said of Grima that she knew many things, and people said
that she was skilled in magic. Now because Christianity was
young and imperfect, many people thought it an accomplishment
for a person to be skilled in magic. Grima's daughter was called Thordis. She
was good-looking and a good worker, and lived at home with her. She
